## Changed

- `Settings… → License` says Upgrade rather than Purchase, like the rest of Meru

## Fixed

- Several new emails arriving at once play the notification sound once, instead of overlapping copies of it
- <kbd>Shift</kbd>-clicking a link to a Gmail page opens it in a new window, instead of showing an error and an empty window
- **Linux:** On Wayland, Meru's window appears when it starts, instead of only when it is opened a second time
- **Meru Pro:** The Pro trial's days left show as whole days, or less than a day, in the titlebar and in `Settings… → License`, instead of fractions like 1.5 day

## Internal Changes

- Updated to Electron 44.9.3, which brings the latest Chrome security fixes

## Added

- **Linux:** Notifications have buttons, as they do on macOS and Windows
  - New email: **Archive**, **Mark as Read**, **Delete** and **Mark as Spam**. GNOME shows the first three
  - A finished download: **Open** or **Show in your file manager**
  - A verification code: **Copy**

## Internal Changes

- Updated to Electron 44, which brings Chrome 152 and its security fixes

## Added

- **Windows:** Meru checks that an update is signed by its publisher before installing it. If an update can't be verified, the titlebar shows `Update not verified`, with a button to download the update and install it yourself

## Changed

- The `Update available` button in the titlebar no longer has an icon, so it takes less room

## Fixed

- `Check for Updates…` says what it found — that Meru is up to date, that an update is available, or that the check couldn't be made — instead of giving no answer
- Restarting to install an update reopens the tabs you had open, the way any other quit does, instead of losing recent changes to them
- **Meru Pro:** During a Pro trial, the days left in the titlebar count down while Meru stays open, and a trial that ends while Meru is open says so in a dialog and in the titlebar, instead of waiting for the next start
- **Meru Pro:** Changing label colors in quick succession leaves only the latest colors in Gmail, instead of sometimes keeping earlier colors alongside them

## Added

- **Windows and Linux:** <kbd>F10</kbd>, or a tap of <kbd>Alt</kbd>, opens the app menu from anywhere in the window, so it no longer takes a click

## Changed

- **macOS:** Downloaded files are marked as coming from the internet, so macOS checks an app, installer or script before it opens, as it does for a download from a browser
- <kbd>Tab</kbd> moves through the page you're on rather than the titlebar and the tab strip around it, the way it already does in Gmail
- Closing Settings, the unified inbox or the download history puts the keyboard back in your mail, so you can type straight away instead of clicking the page first

## Fixed

- Keyboard focus is visible again in Meru's own interface: buttons, switches, checkboxes, tabs and sliders show a focus ring when you <kbd>Tab</kbd> to them
- The close button on the unified inbox and the download history says what it closes, instead of offering to close Settings when Settings isn't open

## Fixed

- **macOS:** Back and forward buttons on a mouse set up with Logi Options+, and a three-finger swipe between pages on a trackpad, now go the right way. In the previous Beta, back went forward and forward went back.

## Changed

- **Meru Pro:** `Settings… → Workspace apps → Windows → Show account label` and `Show account color` are gone. A Workspace apps window now always names its account in its titlebar and window title when you have more than one, and its titlebar shows the account's color, which is what both settings were for.

## Fixed

- **macOS:** Back and forward buttons on a mouse set up with Logi Options+ now go back and forward in Gmail and Workspace apps, as does a three-finger swipe between pages on a trackpad.
- **Meru Pro:** During a Pro trial, the saved searches button appears in the titlebar, instead of staying hidden until a license key is activated.
- **Meru Pro:** A saved search whose query holds a quote, a backslash or a slash, such as `subject:"out of office"`, opens in Gmail instead of doing nothing.
- `Settings… → Updates → Notify when updates are available` takes effect as soon as it is switched, instead of at the next start.
- The notification sound volume slider stops at 5%, the quietest volume Meru plays, instead of going down to a 0% that was ignored.

## Added

- **Meru Pro:** Bitwarden can be installed from `Settings… → Extensions`. It fills and generates passwords and passkeys on Google's sign-in and account pages, offers to save and update logins, and **Open Bitwarden** under its description opens Bitwarden to sign in. Unlocking with biometrics needs the Bitwarden desktop app.
  - Only one password manager can be on at a time. Turning on Bitwarden while 1Password is installed asks first, then turns off 1Password and removes its data, so you'll need to sign in to it again if you switch back.

## Changed

- **Meru Pro:** Switching from the Beta channel back to stable removes any extension that only Beta offers, along with its data. If you return to Beta, you'll need to install it and sign in to it again.

## Fixed

- **Meru Pro:** Downloading a file from a Google Chat conversation saves it, instead of opening an empty tab that left the conversation unresponsive.
- **Meru Pro:** A link that opens in a new tab and turns out to be a download closes that tab and returns you to the one it was opened from, instead of leaving an invisible tab in front of it.

## Added

- Vids, Photos, Apps Script, Analytics, Ads and Search Console now open in Meru as workspace apps, and you can add them to the launcher in `Settings… → Workspace Apps`.
- **Meru Pro:** **Always show trimmed content** in `Settings… → Gmail` shows the quoted text that Gmail hides behind the `•••` button. Off by default.
- **Meru Pro:** **Load clipped messages in full** in `Settings… → Gmail` loads the rest of a long message that Gmail cuts short with “[Message clipped]”. Off by default.

## Fixed

- **Meru Pro:** With **Extend dark theme** on, text you write in a compose window keeps its colors. It no longer turns hard to read when the window is docked, and recipients no longer get it in the dark theme's colors.

## Fixed

- **Linux:** Gmail no longer stays blank or black, shows another account's email, or ignores clicks and typing after Meru starts, after switching accounts or after reopening the window.

## Internal Changes

- Moved Electron back from 44.5.1 to 43.7.7, which brings Chrome 150, until Electron 44 fixes the Linux bug above.

## Added

- **macOS:** Swipe sideways with two fingers on the trackpad to go back and forward in a Gmail tab or a workspace app, as you would in a browser. An arrow slides in from the edge to show where the swipe is heading. It follows `System Settings → Trackpad → More Gestures → Swipe between pages`, and **Swipe between pages** at `Settings… → General` turns it off in Meru alone. On by default.
- **Meru Pro:** Archive, mark as read, delete or mark as spam a message straight from the unified inbox, by hovering its row or with Gmail's own shortcuts: <kbd>E</kbd>, <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>I</kbd>, <kbd>#</kbd> and <kbd>!</kbd>.
- **Meru Pro:** Disable an account at `Settings… → Accounts` to keep it signed in and hidden until you need it again.
- **Meru Pro:** Meru now appears alongside your browsers in your system's default browser settings and in link routers such as Choosey and Finicky, so a rule can send a Google Meet, Chat or Calendar link straight to Meru. Meru opens nothing for a link to anywhere else, so keep the rule to Google's links.
- **Meru Pro:** Meru links can open a Google link in Meru:
  - `meru://open?url=<link>` asks which account should open it when you have more than one.
  - `meru://<email>/open?url=<link>` opens it in that account.
- With Meru itself set as your default browser, a link Meru doesn't open in one of its own tabs now offers to copy itself, since there is no other browser to send it to.
- **Meru Pro:** **Notify for** at `Settings… → Notifications` chooses whether notifications show for all new emails or only the ones Gmail marks as important. Default: all new emails.
- **Meru Pro:** **Show Do Not Disturb button** at `Settings… → Appearance` takes the Do Not Disturb button out of the titlebar when turned off. Do Not Disturb turns off with it, so notifications keep arriving. On by default.
- **Meru Pro:** **Show bookmarks button** at `Settings… → Workspace Apps` takes the bookmarks button out of the titlebar and the vertical tabs sidebar when turned off. On by default.
- Download notifications now have a **Show in Finder** (**Show in File Explorer** on Windows) or **Open** button. Clicking the notification itself brings Meru forward.

## Changed

- **macOS:** Meru now needs macOS 13 (Ventura) or later. Macs on macOS 12 stay on 3.61 and are no longer offered updates.
- **Meru Pro:** The unified inbox now uses less memory and does less work on every check for new mail.

## Fixed

- Clicking a new mail notification opens that email in its account again, instead of only bringing Meru to the front. The notification's **Copy** button for verification codes also works again after the first few seconds.
- Opening an email from a notification, the unified inbox or a Meru link now switches to the account's Gmail tab when another tab was open, instead of opening it out of sight.
- With enough accounts to fill the titlebar, the account buttons now scroll instead of pushing the other titlebar buttons off-screen. Wheel or swipe over the row to move it, or use the arrows at either end; switching accounts brings the one you picked into view.
- The Accounts menu no longer shows shortcuts for accounts past the ninth, which never worked.
- With **Theme** set to **Dark** at `Settings… → Appearance`, the titlebar, tabs and settings no longer sometimes launch light until you switch the setting back and forth.
- After choosing **Later** on an update, the restart prompt no longer returns every few hours for the same version.
- **macOS:** The close, minimize and zoom buttons now sit centered in the titlebar instead of a few pixels too high.
- **macOS:** Showing a download in Finder from its notification no longer opens Finder behind Meru's window.
- **Windows:** The passkey note at `Settings… → Extensions` and the prompt at Google's passkey sign-in now say that only a passkey added to your Google account from inside Meru works, and that passkeys from Chrome, Google Password Manager or your phone don't.
- **Linux and Windows:** **Restart** in Meru's restart prompts now brings Meru back on the AppImage and the portable build, which quit for good instead of restarting.
- **Linux:** Window controls no longer appear over Meru's titlebar buttons on window managers without decorations, such as dwm, i3 and sway. A new **Window controls** setting at `Settings… → Appearance` overrides the detection.

## Internal Changes

- Upgraded Electron from 43.7.0 to 44.5.1, which brings Chrome 152 and its security and performance fixes.

Meru opens nothing for a link to anywhere else, so keep the rule to Google's links.

name: v3.61.0
body:
## Added

- **Meru Pro:** 1Password can now run on sites you add yourself. **Add sites** at `Settings… → Extensions`, beside **Set up desktop app**, lets it sign you in on your company's single sign-on provider as well as on Google's own sign-in pages. Added sites apply after a restart.
- **Linux:** AppImageLauncher, AppImageUpdate, AM and other AppImage tools can now update Meru in place, downloading only the parts that changed rather than the whole file.

## Changed

- **Show Gmail unread badge** at `Settings… → Workspace Apps` replaces **Hide Gmail unread badge when active**. It adds a **Never** choice that hides the unread count on the Gmail tab altogether, alongside **Always** and **When another tab is active**, which is what the old setting did. Your existing choice carries over automatically.
- **Show extensions button** and the titlebar button it showed are gone. The 1Password popup that button opened isn't fully supported in Meru, and 1Password is meant to be used on the sign-in page itself, through its inline menu and the prompts it shows there.
- 1Password's description at `Settings… → Extensions` now says it needs the 1Password desktop app, and is no longer cut off after two lines.
- **Linux:** the AppImage for Intel and AMD machines is now named `Meru-<version>-x86_64.AppImage`, matching the arm64 one.
- **macOS:** on macOS 12 and earlier, this is the last version of Meru. It stops checking for updates there and gets no further fixes, security fixes included, so continued use on those Macs is at your own risk. If you have Meru Pro and can't keep using Meru because of this, email tim@meru.so for a refund.

## Fixed

- **Windows:** Meru can now be made your default mail client. It never appeared under Windows' `Settings → Default apps`, and the switch at `Settings… → General` said Meru was the default while another app kept opening email links. The row now opens Meru's page in Windows Settings, where you can choose it.
- **Windows:** 1Password's **Add Browser** no longer rejects Meru as unsigned. The Windows build is code-signed, so Windows shows Meru's publisher instead of **Unknown publisher**.
- **Windows:** the 1Password setup steps at `Settings… → Extensions` now point to Meru's install folder, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Meru`, instead of `C:\Program Files`, where Meru isn't installed.
- New mail notifications, verification codes included, no longer go missing — not for the first email after launch, not for an email that arrives while you're reading another one, and not for mail Gmail reports late.
- After your computer wakes from sleep or the network changes, the inbox, the unread badge and new mail notifications no longer lag minutes behind your phone. Meru refreshes Gmail as soon as the connection is back, and checks for new mail every 30 seconds until Gmail's own updates have caught up.
- With **Extend dark theme** on, mail you compose in Gmail no longer carries the dark theme's light text colors into drafts and sent messages, which made them unreadable in light-themed mail clients.
- **Help → Report Issue**, **Ask Question** and **Request Feature** now open a compose window that follows **Extend dark theme** and **Close compose window after send**.

## Internal Changes

- Upgraded Electron from 43.5.1 to 43.7.0, picking up the matching Chromium security and performance fixes.

## Added

- **Meru Pro:** Chrome extension support, marked Experimental, at `Settings… → Extensions`. Extensions are off until you turn them on.
  - Only extensions from Meru's curated catalog can be installed. Each one is reviewed for safety and performance before it's listed, and you can request an extension for review to have it added.
  - The catalog starts with 1Password, under **Password Managers**. It signs you in to your Google account with a saved password or passkey, and generates a new one when you change your password or add a passkey in your Google account's security settings. Meru holds no vault data of its own — 1Password answers from the desktop app you connect it to.
  - Extensions are installed from the official Chrome Web Store package, verified before they load, and checked for updates on launch and every three hours. The **Check for updates** button on the page checks on demand.
  - Turning extensions off stops them running without uninstalling them or throwing away the download.
  - **Show extensions button** puts a button in the titlebar that lists your extensions and opens their popups. It's off by default, and you usually won't need it — 1Password's autofill runs in the page, not in the popup.
- Passkey sign-in for Google accounts.
  - **macOS:** **Meru Pro** lets you add a passkey to your Google account from its security settings inside Meru, then sign in with Touch ID — no password manager extension to install. The passkey is stored in the macOS keychain and bound to your Mac's Secure Enclave, so it never leaves the device. Passkeys held in Chrome, iCloud or on your phone don't work here.
  - **Windows:** Google sign-in now uses Windows' own passkey dialog, so Windows Hello, security keys and your synced passkeys work.
- **Meru Pro:** Idle tabs can hibernate to give back the memory they hold, at `Settings… → Workspace Apps`.
  - **Hibernate idle tabs** — Unpinned tabs (default), Selected tabs, or All tabs. A single tab can opt in or out with **Hibernate When Idle** in its context menu.
  - **Hibernate after** — 30 minutes, 1 hour (default), 3 hours, or 6 hours.
  - A hibernated tab keeps its place, title and zoom in the sidebar, and loads again when you click it, back on the page you left with its history intact. The active tab, tabs in their own window, and tabs playing audio are never hibernated.
- Release channels at `Settings… → Updates → Release channel`. Stable is the default; Beta gets upcoming features early and asks for confirmation before switching. You can switch back at any time.
- **Meru Pro:** **Sidebar** as a placement for the launcher and bookmarks at `Settings… → Workspace Apps → Launcher and Bookmarks → Placement`, which keeps the sidebar open even when Gmail is your only tab. Auto (the default) and Titlebar are the other two.
- **Meru Pro:** **Hide promotional banner** at `Settings… → Gmail`, on by default, which hides the recommendation banners above the message list such as the Google Workspace upgrade offer.
- Google Admin joins the Workspace apps.
- Cut, copy and paste now work in Google Docs' own Edit menu.

## Changed

- Verification codes are now copied for you by default, and you choose when at `Settings… → Verification Codes → When to copy`. **Only when you ask** (the default) shows the code in the notification and waits for you to press its Copy button. **As soon as it arrives** copies it the moment the email lands. The notification shows you the code either way.
- Verification codes are now found by a rewritten detector that reads 17 languages and non-Latin scripts — German, Japanese, French, Chinese, Spanish and more — where the old one effectively only understood English.
- <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>,</kbd> on macOS and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>,</kbd> on Windows and Linux now open Meru's settings, matching every other app. Gmail's own settings move to <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>,</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>,</kbd>, which is a new shortcut on Windows and Linux.
- NotebookLM is now **Gemini Notebook**, following Google's rename and its move to `notebook.google.com`. Your saved tabs and bookmarks carry over automatically.
- A wide pass over the interface: clearer confirmation dialogs for destructive actions, errors that say what to do next, and consistent wording throughout menus, dialogs and notifications.
- **macOS:** the Window menu keeps Minimize, Zoom and Bring All to Front; on Windows and Linux it's gone, since Minimize was its only item.

## Fixed

- Downloads: the download-completed notification and the download history entry were both skipped whenever **Open folder when done** was on. Turning that setting on or off no longer needs a restart.
- Cancelling the account picker that opens for a `mailto:` link no longer fails — with two or more accounts, clicking **Cancel** threw instead of closing the picker.

## Internal Changes

- Upgraded Electron from 43.2.0 to 43.5.1, picking up the matching Chromium security and performance fixes.

Tabs landed in 3.58.0 last week, and the feedback that came back was detailed, direct and genuinely useful — this release is mostly the result of it. Sorry for the back and forth it took to get there, the Workspace Apps launcher in particular: it moved to the left of the titlebar in 3.58.0 and moves back to the right here. Thank you for bearing with it, and please keep the feedback coming.

## Changed

- `Settings… → Workspace Apps → Open Behavior` is now **`Mode`**: `Tabs` (default) or `New Windows`. Your setting carries over.
  - `New Windows` opens every app in its own window and hides the tab sidebar. Tabs already open stay open.
  - `Background Tab` is no longer a default — hold <kbd>Cmd</kbd> on macOS, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> on Windows/Linux while clicking. Anyone who had it set lands on `Tabs`.
- The Workspace Apps launcher is back on the right of the titlebar, with a new `Launcher Display` option
  - `Auto` (default) shows one button per app up to three, and collapses into one beyond that. `Collapsed` and `Expanded` pin it either way.
- The launcher and bookmarks buttons move into the tab sidebar while it's visible, and back to the titlebar when it hides
- `Settings… → Appearance → Vertical Tabs` moved to `Settings… → Workspace Apps → Vertical Tabs`, next to the Mode switch. Same options.
- `Open in App` now governs every way an app opens — launcher, links, pinned tabs at launch, reopened tabs, `New … Tab` and `Duplicate`. Off means your default browser, and changing it asks for a restart.
- Bookmarks are saved as URLs rather than flags on a tab, so one reopens where it was saved instead of wherever you browsed to. Existing bookmarks are converted automatically.
- Google My Account opens as a tab like any other app instead of its own window

## Added

- **Meru Pro:** Notifications from Workspace Apps — Calendar reminders and Chat messages now arrive as native notifications, where before they simply never appeared
  - On by default, at `Settings… → Notifications → Workspace Apps`
  - Titled by app, prefixed with the account label when you have more than one: `[Work] Calendar`
  - Clicking one activates the tab it came from, switching account if needed
  - Calendar's are silent, since Calendar plays its own sound
  - Calendar's Snooze button and app icons aren't carried over
- **Meru Pro:** `Open <App> Links in This Tab` in a tab's context menu sends every link to that app into that tab, the way Gmail already works
  - One tab per app — designating a second asks first and names the tab that loses it
  - Marked in the sidebar; `Vertical Tabs → Show App Links Badge` (on) hides the mark, not the behavior
  - Kept across restarts on pinned tabs, for the session on unpinned ones
- Bookmarks have a proper home: a titlebar button — or one at the foot of the tab sidebar while it's visible — opens a popup listing the account's bookmarks
  - Bookmark the current page with the star on a tab row, in a Workspace App window's titlebar, or from the tab's context menu. It fills while the page is bookmarked and empties as you browse on.
  - Drag rows to reorder, ✕ on hover to remove
- **Meru Pro:** A width button at the foot of the tab sidebar switches it between narrow and wide
  - It lasts for this run of the app on that account and leaves your `Width` setting alone; `Reset Width` in the sidebar's context menu hands it back
  - `Vertical Tabs → Show Width Button` (on) hides it
- **Meru Pro:** `Vertical Tabs → Show Windows` (on) lists apps open in their own window in the sidebar, where clicking one brings its window forward
- **Meru Pro:** `Vertical Tabs → Hide Unread Badge When Active` (off) drops Gmail's unread count from its tab while you're on it. The attention icon still shows.
- The tab sidebar scrolls once it fills, keeping the controls at its foot reachable. Pinned and open tabs scroll separately, and pinned tabs can't squeeze the open ones below three rows.
- Close the current tab with <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>W</kbd> on macOS, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>W</kbd> on Windows/Linux. <kbd>Cmd</kbd>/<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>W</kbd> still closes the window.
- Jump to a pinned tab with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd>, Gmail counting as the first
- `Load on Launch` is now in a Workspace App window's More Options menu, reaching `New Windows` mode

## Fixed

- Sheets, Slides and Forms all showed up as Docs — they share `docs.google.com` and were told apart by domain alone. Each now gets its own icon, title, zoom level and `Open in App` exclusion.
  - Bookmarks saved before this update keep their Docs icon until saved again
- Presenting in Slides and going fullscreen in Meet now work, and the page covers the titlebar and tab sidebar instead of leaving them on screen
- Workspace Apps were told notifications were allowed even with the setting off, so pages showed no blocked state while their notifications went nowhere. Permissions Meru didn't handle also never settled, leaving pages waiting forever.
- Picking an audio output device in Google Meet now works
- **Windows/Linux:** new-mail notifications never showed the email summary and the `Show Summary` switch wasn't offered. It now sits below the subject, with the switch to turn it off.
- Verification-code auto-copy only scanned what the notification displayed, so turning off `Show Subject` or `Show Summary` could stop it working. It reads the whole email now.
- Quitting with the bookmarks or recent downloads popup open could hang the app

## Changed

- Google Apps are now called **Workspace Apps** throughout the app — `Settings… → Google Apps` is now `Settings… → Workspace Apps`, and the notification option moved along with it. Your existing settings carry over automatically.
- `Pinned Apps` are now `Launcher Apps` and open from a single Workspace Apps launcher in the titlebar instead of one icon per app
- `Always Open in New Window` has been replaced by the new `Open Behavior` option
- `Full Dark Theme` is now `Extend Dark Theme` and has moved from Experimental to Beta.
- Saved searches moved to the right side of the titlebar and now open in a dropdown instead of a toggled list
- Download History is no longer buried in Settings — it opens as its own full-width view from `View → Downloads` (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>L</kbd> on macOS, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>L</kbd> on Windows/Linux), matching how the Unified Inbox is presented
- <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> now switch tabs instead of accounts
  - **macOS:** cycle accounts with <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>]</kbd> and <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>[</kbd>
  - **Windows/Linux:** cycling accounts no longer has a shortcut — select an account directly with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd> on Windows, <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd> on Linux
- Zoom in, out and reset now apply to whichever tab or window is in front instead of every Gmail view at once. Your existing Gmail zoom level is preserved.

## Added

- **Meru Pro:** Workspace Apps now open as tabs inside the main window instead of always taking over a separate window
  - A vertical tab sidebar appears on the left as soon as a second tab is open, and stays hidden while Gmail is the only tab
  - Gmail is always the first tab and carries its unread count, or a warning icon when the account needs attention
  - `Settings… → Workspace Apps → Open Behavior` controls how apps open: `Tab` (default), `New Window`, or `Background Tab`
  - Hold <kbd>Cmd</kbd> on macOS, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> on Windows/Linux to open a background tab, add <kbd>Shift</kbd> for a foreground tab, or hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> alone to open a new window
  - Switch tabs with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd> and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd>, reopen the last closed tab with <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> on macOS, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> on Windows/Linux
  - Close a tab with middle click or its close button, and drag tabs to reorder them
  - Keep tabs around across restarts by pinning or bookmarking them
    - Pinned tabs sit in their own section above the rest; bookmarked tabs collect in a Bookmarks section at the bottom once closed
    - Closing a pinned or bookmarked tab dims it instead of removing it — click it again to load it back
    - `Load on Launch` in a pinned tab's context menu decides whether it loads at startup or waits until you open it
    - A pinned or bookmarked tab that was living in its own window comes back in a window
  - Tab context menu with `New … Tab`, `Reload`, `Duplicate`, `Move to New Window` / `Move to Tab`, `Copy Link`, `Open in Default Browser`, `Pin` / `Unpin`, `Bookmark` / `Remove Bookmark`, `Close`, `Close Other Tabs` and `Close Tabs Below`. Right-clicking empty space in the sidebar offers `Reopen Closed Tab`.
  - Move a tab out into its own window and back again — a tab that has been moved out stays in the sidebar with a window badge, and Workspace App windows have a `Move to Tab` entry in their titlebar menu
  - `Settings… → Appearance → Vertical Tabs → Width` sets how wide the tab sidebar is
    - `Auto` (default) switches between narrow and wide based on the open tabs, or pick `Narrow` or `Wide`
  - `Settings… → Workspace Apps → Persist Zoom` remembers each app's zoom level across restarts (on by default). Each app keeps one zoom level, shared by all of its tabs and windows.
